topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the intended learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional cancer treatment modalities that physically remove or non-specifically damage rapidly dividing cells.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific vulnerabilities and molecular defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies that selectively target cancer cells by taking advantage of their hormone dependence, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the development, therapeutic application, and resistance pathways associated with small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenic kinases.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and mechanisms of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates used to target cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and cell-based immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the evidence for natural immune surveillance and various therapeutic strategies that recruit or re-engineer immune cells to fight cancer.

topics.label: Challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the ongoing clinical challenges, historical outcomes, and strategic considerations shaping the future of cancer treatment.
